correctness.rationale: On each invariant axis, divide the second-iterate displacement by the first-iterate displacement. The resulting quadratic has two distinct positive roots precisely for R>2; neither is a fixed point, so they are exchanged. At R=2 they merge at the fixed point 1. Cyclic permutation accounts for exactly three positive axis-supported primitive cycles (not for any off-axis orbit). Multiplying the triangular axial Jacobians yields 5−R² and the two absent-coordinate factors p_R(c). The longitudinal sink inequality gives 2<R<√6; within it p_R<1 exactly on (1,R), and the minimum crosses −1 at the simple root of R³−3R−6. This produces the excluded point, then the excluded closed band; the width follows from the simple-root Taylor expansion. The four-component assertion is for fixed R in R_*≤R<√6, as dictated by the preceding full-space criterion; for R≥√6 the sink locus is empty. At u_+ the one-step absent-coordinate factor vanishes at q=(1+R)/(R u_+), and 1<q<(R+1)/2 with p_R(q)=0. For both interactions strictly between 1 and q, all per-capita factors are positive near both phases (including the resident factor, whose cycle ratio is positive). Local attraction and a small trapping neighborhood for F² whose first image lies near the other phase then give an open set of strictly positive orbits. If either interaction exceeds q, continuity makes the corresponding one-step factor negative near u_+, which any orbit converging to the two-cycle must visit. No claim is made at q, about nonlinear unit-multiplier stability, or for global positivity preservation.

originality.rationale: The logistic axis orbit and the shifted quadratic reentrance mechanism are known ingredients. The closest prior finding gives literally the same quadratic after translation and derives the same critical cubic for synchronous cycles of the same map. The supported distinct contribution is identifying it with the two independent axial invasion multipliers and classifying the actual boundary sinks together with their separate strictly positive forward accessibility barrier. No examined stronger claim gives that axial/accessibility theorem.
residual_risks: The full 2001 Blackmore–Chen–Perez–Savescu article was not accessible and may contain stronger axial analysis. Bischi–Tramontana was available but inspected in the relevant sections rather than exhaustively. The originality verdict is bounded, not certified priority.

value.rationale: The boundary cycles model species exclusion under pulsed dynamics. Their two-step multiplier can have modulus less than one even though a small positive absent population is driven negative at one phase. The explicit threshold and local positive trapping versus exclusion answer when a real-space sink is dynamically reachable within the strict positive cone. That distinction is useful and not a mere recitation of logistic period doubling or the shifted synchronous stability polynomial.
